digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure — subprocess and network sentinels
propositions: Test-only timeout windows in subprocess reap and network sentinel tests are unnecessarily large, causing tests to spend 1–2s waiting for injected deadlines to expire.

Three reap tests depend on child-side setup (pidfile creation, spawn counter, partial stdout flush) completing before the timeout deadline, but ordering is implicit in wall-clock values rather than explicit gates, creating a load-dependent race.

The blanket autouse fixture applies a single 1s timeout to all tests in test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py, but the read-retry test requires a generous ceiling to complete two sequential child processes, while reap tests require a short deadline to ensure the child hangs.
The 2s low-speed window in tight_stall exceeds the 1s minimum that git http.lowSpeedTime supports and the 1s window already proven by the dribble test, adding unnecessary latency.

Explicit readiness gates (file markers polled by parent-side wrapper) must replace implicit timing assumptions so that child-setup completion is observed before the injected window begins, removing load dependence.
